title: POC weekly sync - model selection and pinning
summary: Weekly POC sync to review evaluation results across candidate models, discuss pinning strategy and fallbacks, and align next steps for performance benchmarks and security docs. Customer saw good quality on redwood-7b-v2 and mistral-instruct variants; latency/cost tradeoffs remain the key constraint. Agreed to pin a quantized variant for user-facing routes and keep a higher-quality FP16 variant as a fallback for complex cases. Action items assigned for benchmarks, pricing, security evidence, and schedule for next canary test.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-02 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42 minutes | Attendees: Jordan, Priya, Marcus (Redwood); Alicia, Tom, Mei, Ravi (StellarHealth)

[00:00] Jordan: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, uh it's Jordan from Redwood, and this is Priya our solutions engineer and Marcus on success. quick agenda — review your eval numbers, talk pinning, and next steps for the canary.

[00:12] Alicia: thanks, Jordan. quick note we had a heads-up from execs, timeline is still end of month for a production pilot, so we want decisions this week ideally.

[00:22] Priya: got it. we looked at the eval spreadsheet you shared, quick summary — redwood-7b-v2-fp16 had best helpfulness on the prompt set, mistral-instruct-7b was close on instruction compliance, and the q4 quant variant redwood-7b-v2-q4 reduced token latency and cost by about 40% but had occasional hallucination on long-context tests.

[00:45] Tom: yeah that's what we saw, the q4 model's tail latency is way better at our 512 token median, but for long reports it sometimes repeats or invents numbers.

[00:58] Priya: right, that's expected tradeoff with aggressive quant; our recommendation is to pin the q4 variant for the high-throughput user-facing endpoints and route complex, high-stakes prompts to the fp16 variant. you can do that via per-route model pinning in the catalog config.

[01:18] Mei: from a security angle, two questions — first, do pinned versions remain immutable in Dedicated/private? second, about audit logs and KMS usage for keys in the private deploy.

[01:28] Marcus: good q. pinned versions are immutable once pinned in the deployment config; you can unpin and roll forward but the audit log records the change. on Private we integrate with customer KMS and HSM for model keys and we surface audit events in Redwood Console — we can send the SOC2 evidence pack after the call.

[01:48] Alicia: awesome, please send that.

[02:02] Ravi: can you clarify fallback behavior? if the q4 variant fails quality checks mid-flight will the system automatically fall back to the fp16?

[02:10] Priya: yes you can configure automatic fallback policies: threshold by score or token confidence and fallback to a compatible variant (we call them compatible family variants). we also support canary overrides and circuit-breaker rules by error rate or latency. note however that switching mid-request isn't possible — fallback happens at request routing, so we recommend short time windows for detection.

[02:36] Tom: sounds good. one thing — our infra team wants to measure cost per 1k responses. any guidance numbers?

[02:43] Jordan: rough numbers from your pilot usage: redwood-7b-v2-q4 comes in about 0.6x cost relative to the fp16, and latency is around 65% of fp16 on the same GPU stack. we'll give you the detailed per-token breakdown in the pricing doc.

[03:01] Alicia: I noticed a weird spike in latency on Friday at 3pm region, is that capacity?

[03:07] Priya: likely routing to a higher load host or a fallback to a bigger model; we'll pull logs. sometimes the autoscaler triggers a fallback to a different pool if the dedicated pool is saturated, but we'll check the trace.

[03:22] Mei: FYI we have regulatory constraints for PHI, so any external logging must be disabled for routes that handle clinical notes. can Redwood support per-route retention settings?

[03:31] Marcus: yes — per-route retention and redaction are supported on Dedicated and Private. we can configure zero retention for specific endpoints. we'll add a config snippet to the security pack.

[03:45] Ravi: back to pinning — what is the recommended naming for model variants in the catalog so we avoid ambiguity?

[03:52] Priya: we suggest semantic names: redwood-7b-v2-fp16, redwood-7b-v2-q4, mistral-instruct-7b-1.1, etc. and use catalog aliases in your route config like patient-summaries-prod -> redwood-7b-v2-q4. that makes rollbacks straightforward: alias -> different version.

[04:12] Alicia: ok let's talk about rollback testing — we want an automated rollback plan if the canary shows quality regression. how does Redwood handle that?

[04:20] Priya: typically you'd run a canary with a small percentage of traffic to the new variant and keep the previous pinned variant as the fallback. Redwood Console can auto-rollback based on eval metrics you push — we support webhook based eval ingestion so your evaluation harness can trigger rollbacks.

[04:38] Tom: is eval ingestion currently live in our project?

[04:42] Marcus: not yet, but we set up the webhook URL in staging. Priya, I think you had a note to finalize the schema?

[04:50] Priya: yes I'll send the schema, it's a simple json with prompt id, reference score, model score, and pass/fail. there may be minor mapping typos in the sample we sent — apologies, that was OCR noise from the doc.

[05:03] Alicia: ok thanks.

[05:10] [05:10] Customer question: competitor comparison, we evaluated Anthropic and Vertex — where does Redwood fit on latency/cost?

[05:18] Jordan: short answer — Redwood gives you more predictable cost for open model variants and advanced routing to trade latency and quality. Anthropic/OpenAI have strong models but higher cost and less control over routing and model pinning. Vertex is similar on infra but you’d build more of the ops stack yourself. competitors mentioned: Anthropic, OpenAI, Vertex AI.

[05:42] Ravi: are there any known issues with the redwood-7b-v2-q4 quant on our dataset? we saw numeric hallucination in the financial tables.

[05:50] Priya: quant can degrade numeric fidelity; mitigation options: enable post-processing validation, route numeric extraction through a structured tool call, or use the fp16 variant for those specific endpoints. we can show an example rule in the console.

[06:08] Tom: can we run a focused benchmark on numeric-heavy prompts? we'd like tail-latency at p95 and quality metrics.

[06:14] Priya: yes — action: run a benchmark with your 200 numeric-critical prompts and we'll return p50/p95 cost and quality numbers.

[06:22] Alicia: timeline?

[06:25] Priya: we can run it in 48 hours once you drop the prompt set to the bucket.

[06:30] Jordan: for the pilot decision, proposed config: pin redwood-7b-v2-q4 as primary for patient-summary-route, use redwood-7b-v2-fp16 as fallback; enable auto-fallback on quality threshold 0.7 and set canary at 5% traffic for 24h. does that sound ok?

[06:50] Ravi: yes that seems reasonable.

[07:00] Mei: just to confirm — audit logs for pin changes will show user and timestamp?

[07:06] Marcus: yes full audit trail, and we can forward logs to your SIEM via syslog or cloud logging.

[07:14] Alicia: perfect.

[07:20] [07:20] Quick recap and next steps list readout

[07:25] Jordan: recap: 1) run numeric benchmark (customer -> provide 200 prompts), 2) Redwood to run p50/p95 and cost delta for q4 vs fp16, 3) Priya to send webhook schema and config snippet for per-route pinning and retention, 4) Marcus to share SOC2+KMS docs and audit log examples, 5) Jordan to share pricing and formal pilot proposal.

[07:45] Alicia: and timeline for each?

[07:48] Jordan: numeric benchmark in 48 hours after prompt drop, pricing and pilot doc by 2027-03-05, security pack same day, canary scheduled once benchmarks are in — aim for 2027-03-09 for canary.

[08:05] Tom: small nit — please include example config for alias-based rollback. that helps our infra template.

[08:10] Priya: yes will include an alias example and a rollback playbook.

[08:16] Mei: last question — are there known regional model availability differences? we operate EMEA and US.

[08:22] Jordan: some models have region-specific variant availability due to licensing; we can confirm for redwood-7b-v2-q4 in EU region — note, there was a recent infra patch that changed kernel selection which caused a small perf delta last month, but that's been resolved.

[08:38] Alicia: ok thanks everyone. any other blockers?

[08:42] Ravi: none from product.

[08:44] Marcus: I'll follow up in CRM with the action items and attach the docs.

[08:50] Jordan: great — thanks all, we'll send the deliverables and sync next Tuesday.

[41:30] [end of call]

Note: transcript contains occasional auto-transcription errors (typos, name variants, misheard acronyms).
